title: app chart values
description: Helm validates the merged values against this schema on lint, template, install and upgrade. Every object closes with additionalProperties:false or a typed additionalProperties, so an unknown key is a failed release rather than a setting that silently did nothing.

environment.description: Which environment this release is. Mirrors the EksStack instances in aws/cdk/bin/app.ts; adding a third means adding it here, adding values-<env>.yaml, and adding it to ENVIRONMENTS in tools/audit-helm-values.ts.

nameOverride.description: Replaces the chart-name half of generated resource names.

replicaCount.description: Desired pods when autoscaling.enabled is false. With the HPA on, the Deployment renders no replicas field at all and this value does not reach the cluster — npm run audit:helm keeps it inside the HPA's range so that turning autoscaling off is not also a change of capacity.

autoscaling.description: Horizontal Pod Autoscaler. Scales pods against CPU utilization; the Cluster Autoscaler in EksStack scales the nodes underneath. docs/autoscaling.md derives every threshold here.

minReplicas.description: The HPA's floor, and the number the PodDisruptionBudget is checked against when autoscaling is on. Kubernetes requires at least 1 without the HPAScaleToZero feature gate, which EKS does not enable.

maxReplicas.description: The ceiling. Must exceed minReplicas — checked by npm run audit:helm, since JSON Schema cannot compare two properties — and maxReplicas × resources.requests.cpu must fit what the Cluster Autoscaler's maximum node count can supply, or the HPA scales into Pending pods.

targetCPUUtilizationPercentage.description: Percentage of the CPU request, not of the limit or the node. The gap between this and the service's latency knee is the headroom that covers the ~90s between load arriving and a new pod serving.

targetMemoryUtilizationPercentage.description: Optional, and usually wrong when requests.memory equals limits.memory: a runtime that holds freed pages sits near its target permanently, so the HPA scales up and never back down. Set it only for a service whose memory tracks concurrency.

allOf.description: A scale-down with no stabilization window removes pods on the first low sample and adds them back on the next, which turns ordinary traffic noise into a rollout. Kubernetes itself defaults to 300s; this chart's floor is 60s, deliberately lower than that default so a service with a genuinely short trough can opt into a faster one without editing the schema.

tag.description: Immutable image tag. Moving tags are rejected: with one, the running image depends on when a pod last restarted, so two pods in a ReplicaSet can serve different code and a rollback has no fixed target to return to.

imagePullSecrets.description: Names of image pull secrets. Empty for ECR, which is authorised through the node role.

name.description: Defaults to the release fullname when empty. Must be set when create is false.

annotations.description: eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn goes here, bound to a role whose trust policy names this namespace and service account.

type.description: ClusterIP unless something outside the cluster reaches this Service directly. Ingress is a later Phase 8 item and terminates at a ClusterIP Service.

resources.description: Required, not optional. No requests means BestEffort scheduling and first eviction under node pressure; no memory limit means one leaking container can evict every other pod on the node.

limits.description: A memory limit is required and a CPU limit is not: memory is incompressible, while a CPU limit adds CFS throttling latency to a service that is not otherwise short of CPU.

config.description: Rendered into a ConfigMap and injected with envFrom. Values must be strings: ConfigMap data is string-valued, so an unquoted 8080 is rejected by the API server at apply time — here it is rejected at lint time instead.

extraEnv.description: Environment variables that are not plain configuration — a downward-API field, or one that must be ordered after envFrom.

podDisruptionBudget.description: What makes a node drain wait for a replacement pod instead of taking the last healthy replica.

minAvailable.description: A count, not a percentage, so its meaning does not change when replicaCount does. Must stay below replicaCount — a budget equal to the replica count blocks every drain forever, which stops cluster upgrades rather than protecting the service. Checked against replicaCount by npm run audit:helm, which the schema cannot do because JSON Schema cannot compare two properties.

strategy.description: RollingUpdate parameters. maxUnavailable 0 keeps capacity flat through a rollout, at the cost of one extra pod for its duration.

terminationGracePeriodSeconds.description: Must exceed the longest in-flight request, or every deploy truncates responses.

hpaScalingRules.description: One direction of an HPA's behavior. The two policy kinds are named keys rather than the API's array, because Helm replaces arrays wholesale: an environment file changing one policy in a list would have to restate the others, and the one it forgot would vanish.

stabilizationWindowSeconds.description: The window the HPA takes its most conservative recommendation from. Absent is not the same as 0: absent falls back to the API default, which is 0 for scale-up and 300 for scale-down. The chart always renders it, so it is required here.

selectPolicy.description: Which policy wins when both percent and pods are set: Max takes the larger change, Min the smaller, Disabled blocks movement in this direction entirely. Irrelevant with a single policy.

hpaScalingPolicy.description: How much the HPA may move the replica count in one period, in percent of the current count or in absolute pods.

cpuQuantity.description: Kubernetes CPU quantity: cores (1, 1.5) or millicores (500m).

memoryQuantity.description: Kubernetes memory quantity. Binary suffixes (Mi, Gi) are what the API server reports back, so using them keeps values and observed limits comparable.

countOrPercent.description: An absolute pod count or a percentage string, which is what the Deployment API accepts.

probe.description: An HTTP GET probe against the container's named http port.
